profile.name: Luigi Scofano de Araujo
profile.headline: Curiosity in code.
profile.intro: I am an undergraduate Computer Engineering student at Poli-USP. I explore artificial intelligence and data by building applications, experiments, and tools that turn ideas into something tangible.
about: I enjoy understanding how things work: how an algorithm chooses a move, how an image becomes information, and how to organize data without losing its context.
My path connects academic research, software development, and data analysis. I am currently deepening my studies in machine learning, generative AI, and data engineering.
I am also a jiu-jitsu instructor. Teaching is part of how I approach my projects: clear explanations, practice, and room to learn through experimentation.
profile.photoAlt: Luigi Scofano in a seaside landscape, with a small pixel-art great kiskadee in the photo
aboutOverview: I am Luigi Scofano de Araujo, a Computer Engineering student at Poli-USP. I am interested in artificial intelligence and data, especially in understanding how algorithms work and turning that knowledge into applications that other people can use and explore. I enjoy investigating how a program chooses a move, how an image can become information, and how to organize data without losing the context of where it came from.

In my undergraduate research at IME-USP, I studied natural language processing and optical character recognition applied to Old Tupi, supervised by Professor Marcelo Finger. The work combined organizing and reviewing historical sources, preserving spelling, traceability and distinguishing software suggestions from human decisions. I also contribute to a virtual museum of computing at LASSu-USP, a laboratory coordinated by Professor Tereza Cristina Melo de Brito Carvalho.

My projects turn this curiosity into games, tools and experiments. Intuição brings together 19 games with a Brazilian identity; GestureLab explores hands, gestures and poses through computer vision; Pokédex organizes a catalog for exploring species and forms. In Trilha Viva, I develop study organization, PDF processing and source-based review, distinguishing working local features from AI and account integrations that are still pending.

My experience connects computing with practical needs: dashboards and data analysis at Núclea, front-end collaboration on an international transactions platform at BTG Pactual, and an AI-assisted prospecting platform used by the TRIA Commodities team. I also participated in AMPHIBIA USP’s Projects area and developed academic work in software, numerical methods, algorithms, digital circuits and FPGA.

Outside computing, I teach jiu-jitsu and self-defense and served as the sport’s director at Poli-USP’s athletics association. I also volunteered as a mathematics and Portuguese teacher at ACEP. Teaching shapes how I build: explain clearly, encourage practice, listen to users and leave room to learn through experimentation.

projects.name: Intuição
projects.subtitle: Learning through discovery
projects.type: Independent project · Classical AI and games
projects.summary: Logic, geometry, and strategy games that turn concepts into visible decisions. The AI calculates its moves directly in the browser.
projects.details: A platform with 19 games across Intuition, Logical Reasoning and Versus. Its Brazilian visual identity includes tiles, mascots and individual game illustrations. DESVIO uses exact search with memoization on supported maps; CERCO combines minimax, alpha-beta pruning and heuristics.
projects.contribution: Development of mechanics, levels, interface, hints, and documentation. The repository distinguishes original code, visual assets, and third-party credits.
projects.limitation: Classical game AI, with no generative model. CERCO uses a bounded search and does not guarantee perfect play; BROTO is a two-player duel, with no bot in this version.
projects.imageAlt: Official Intuição wordmark with blue, yellow and green tiles
projects.caption: Official site wordmark

projects.name: Undergraduate Research · Tupi Antigo
projects.subtitle: From historical source to data
projects.summary: Tools for structuring and reviewing lexicographic data while preserving sources, original spelling, and human review decisions.
projects.details: A TSV pipeline for importing, NFC normalization, auditing, and exporting, with CER/WER metrics and optional OCR via Tesseract. Research supervised by Professor Marcelo Finger, PhD.
projects.contribution: Research and tools documented by Luigi. The documentation acknowledges the academic partnership with Calebe Rezende’s Dicionário Tupi-Português.
projects.limitation: The demo uses fictional records. The repository does not distribute the complete validated corpus or provide automatic sentence translation.
projects.caption: Project cover; not an OCR result.

projects.name: Kaggle-oRF
projects.subtitle: Decisions in different directions
projects.summary: An oblique decision forest implementation for investigating boundaries that combine multiple features at each node.
projects.details: Coursework for PCS 3838, Artificial Intelligence, at Poli-USP. Includes orthogonal and oblique trees, forests, and prediction export. Each node learns its directions through PCA/SVD and selects splits based on information gain.
projects.contribution: A collaborative academic project. The implementation and contribution history are available in the repository; it is not presented as solely authored work.
projects.limitation: A demonstration using synthetic data. No score, Kaggle ranking, or experimental competition results are presented. The figure is educational, not a benchmark.
projects.imageAlt: Educational figure comparing orthogonal and oblique splits across points from two classes
projects.caption: Educational illustration from the repository · Not an experimental result

projects.name: GestureLab
projects.subtitle: Movement as an interface
projects.summary: A webcam-based lab for tracking hands, recognizing gestures, drawing in the air, and comparing poses with a local catalog.
projects.details: Four independent modes: hands, gestures, airwrite, and posematch. The application connects detected coordinates to interaction states, stroke smoothing, export, and geometric comparison.
projects.contribution: Integration, interaction logic, local interface, geometric descriptor, reproducible catalog, and tests. The detection models are pretrained MediaPipe models.
projects.limitation: No custom models are trained, and air writing does not include word recognition. The pose preview uses synthetic input and does not represent a performance measurement.
projects.imageOmissionReason: No verified standalone project logo or suitable documentary image; interface previews intentionally omitted.

projects.name: Pokédex
projects.subtitle: Data to explore
projects.summary: An interface for exploring species, forms, evolutions, and game-specific information, with versioned data and reproducible imports.
projects.details: A searchable catalog with filters, browser-stored favorites, Shiny mode, stats, and evolution families. The original Java exercise remains in a separate module.
projects.contribution: A fan application developed by Luigi, with a responsive interface, data preparation, tests, and documentation. Sources for data and images are identified in the repository.
projects.limitation: Queries reflect the coverage of the imported dataset. Favorites are stored in the browser. Pokémon and its assets belong to their respective rights holders; this is an unofficial project.
projects.imageAlt: Original icon from the Pokédex fan project; not an application screenshot
projects.caption: Original project icon · fan project, not official

projects.name: Digital Laboratory
projects.subtitle: From code to circuit
projects.summary: FPGA circuits and games that connect state machines, sensors, serial communication, and computer interfaces.
projects.details: A collection from Poli-USP’s Digital Laboratory I and II courses, with experiments and the Math Genius and Guardião do Paredão projects. Includes source files, reports, simulations, and verification tools.
projects.contribution: Group projects, with authorship, teaching materials, and subsequent organization identified in the repository’s implementation documentation.
projects.limitation: Simulation and compilation are not equivalent to hardware validation. Physical validation of the revisions in this edition remains pending; no claims of therapeutic effectiveness are made.
projects.imageAlt: Control and datapath diagram reproduced from the LabDig documentation; not physical hardware validation
projects.caption: Documentation diagram · not a hardware photograph or validation

projects.name: Trilha Viva
projects.subtitle: Materials, sources and review
projects.summary: Study organization with texts, PDFs, references and review planning.
projects.details: PDF extraction, optional local OCR, editable topics and questions, human review, tasks, history and backups. The demo stores data in the browser.
projects.contribution: Product, interface, material organization, reference validation, local persistence and integration documentation.
projects.limitation: AI, external automations, accounts and synchronization are not active in the demo. Demonstration content is not real generation; references require review.
projects.imageAlt: Official Trilha Viva Pages symbol B, shown with the same crop as the application
projects.caption: Official symbol B · original artwork, not a screen preview

projects.name: Métodos Numéricos
projects.subtitle: Mathematics through experiments
projects.summary: Reproducible experiments exploring precision, convergence and numerical stability.
projects.details: Seven tracks covering Python, Newton and fractals, floating point and PLU, DFT/FFT, interpolation, ODEs and Chua, and synthetic GPS.
projects.contribution: Implementations, notebooks, plots and tests, with documented academic context and sources.
projects.limitation: Results depend on each experiment’s parameters and assumptions; the GPS example uses synthetic data.
projects.imageAlt: Convergence plot produced by the Numerical Methods experiments

projects.name: Tetris em C
projects.subtitle: Rules and replay in the terminal
projects.summary: A terminal game with an engine separated from its interface and reproducible matches.
projects.details: Seven pieces, movement, rotation, scoring, levels, pause and seeded replay; rule and command-line tests.
projects.contribution: Portfolio implementation, separation of engine and interface, and match verification, with documented provenance.
projects.limitation: Requires a C11 compiler and compatible terminal; it is not a web application.
projects.imageOmissionReason: No verified standalone project logo or suitable documentary image; interface previews intentionally omitted.

projects.name: Sistemas Digitais II
projects.subtitle: Control and datapath
projects.summary: Educational projects connecting numerical representation, instructions and processor architecture.
projects.details: Binary-to-BCD Double-Dabble converter, programmable calculator with a custom ISA, and a RISC-V subset core, testbenches and waveforms.
projects.contribution: Academic control and datapath projects, supported by simulations and architecture documentation.
projects.limitation: The core implements an educational subset, not a complete RISC-V processor; simulation does not establish physical validation.
projects.imageAlt: Signal waveform from the Double-Dabble simulation for input 42

projects.name: Sistemas de Programação
projects.subtitle: From instruction to execution
projects.summary: A postfix calculator and educational tools for understanding stacks, subroutines and memory.
projects.details: Python assembler and executor, byte reader, stack and RPN calculator in MVN Assembly, with execution tracing.
projects.contribution: Academic routines, educational machine, examples and tests separating assembly from execution.
projects.limitation: MVN is an educational machine; the simulator does not represent a commercial processor.
projects.imageAlt: Documentation cover for Programming Systems; not a runtime screenshot

projects.name: Algoritmos e estruturas de dados
projects.subtitle: Invariants and complexity
projects.summary: Algorithmic problems explored through contracts, tests and boundary cases.
projects.details: Gene search, interval union and pair counting in Java; an independent C11 extension on the Collatz sequence.
projects.contribution: Implementations and organization of exercises, demonstrations and validators with academic context.
projects.limitation: Examples check defined cases and do not prove general properties such as the Collatz conjecture.
projects.imageAlt: Educational interval-union figure from the algorithms project

projects.name: Programação Orientada a Objetos
projects.subtitle: Objects, events and states
projects.summary: Exercises exploring responsibilities, composition, persistence and state transitions.
projects.details: Event agenda and fictional simulation, State/CSV studies and multisets; historical materials separated from newer implementations.
projects.contribution: Organization of academic exercises, object modeling, executable examples and tests.
projects.limitation: The simulation uses a fictional setting; historical materials may have different requirements from the current suite.
projects.imageAlt: Documentation cover for Object-Oriented Programming; not an application screenshot

projects.name: MAC0321 · Lista 08
projects.subtitle: Interfaces and design patterns
projects.summary: Exercises in graphical interfaces, testing and adapting collections through composition.
projects.details: Swing factorial interface, JUnit tests, collection wrappers, Adapter and string operations.
projects.contribution: Exercises coauthored with Hugo Spadete Arrivabene, preserving context and authorship.
projects.limitation: Some exercises require a graphical environment; this is neither a web application nor solely authored work.
projects.imageAlt: Educational Swing and Adapter diagram based on Lista 08 classes; not an application screenshot
